newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mostly lower, nearby meal up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mostly lower, nearby meal up.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended mostly lower on Monday amid outlooks for wetter weather next week in the U.S. Midwest but nearby soymeal closed higher on the lack of deliveries, traders said.

"In the August meal, the lack of deliveries continue to be the feature there but most of the spec business is all out," said Jerry Gidel, analyst with Dean Witter. "The soybean oil just had sluggish tones from palm oil and there's no big talk of any overseas interest right now."
New crop months ended lower after meteorologists predicted a wetter pattern next week for the U.S. Midwest.

"This morning's (Monday) computer guidance indicates that by this weekend and next week (the week of August 11) there will be some changes in the pattern," Smith Barney's Jon Davis wrote. "Plain and simply, this pattern is much more favorable for widespread rains in the central U.S.," he added.
The National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook, released Monday afternoon, also called for below normal temperatures and above normal precipitation for Illinois.
Soymeal ended $4.30 per ton higher to $3.90 lower with December down $3.30 at $213.30. Soyoil closed 0.21 to 0.12 cent per lb lower with December down 0.15 at 22.59.
Rains in China also drew bearish reviews.
"Beans got whacked because of the good rains that occured across the northern provinces of China," Dean Witter's Gidel said. "We've stablized those conditions for a while."

On the day, Refco Inc and Merrill Lynch each sold 500 lots December soymeal while Griffin Trading and ING each sold 200 December. Merrill Lynch bought 300 August and Smith Barney and Prudential Securities each bought 200 August.
In soyoil, Refco sold 600 December, Produce Grain sold 400 December and Smith Barney sold 300 December and 100 September, pit sources said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 27,000 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 27,793 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 20,000 lots, against Thursday's 24,492.
